brief: The courtyard has never had a New element in the loop (the cell is empty) and the town runs on the sun (sunVec(), sunArc, warmth) but nothing in the courtyard reads the hour. Put a sundial in the courtyard — a low stone plinth and gnomon on the grass inside the bed ring (a cell off the RING at a spot with no bench, no desire path, checked against wear[] and BENCH_SPOTS), whose cast shadow is drawn per frame from sunVec() at the same hardness the cast shadows use (shadowF/shSpread), so it fades under a grey lid and vanishes at night. Its footprint goes into buildGrid() as one non-walkable cell (a new tile kind or WALL-at-ground — the census's tileKinds/structures are EXPECTED to move; re-pin the baseline and say so). Name it in nameAt with the hour it reads: 'the sundial — about ten'. Walkers already route around non-walkable cells.
successLooksLike: Warp to 08:00, 12:00 and 16:00 on one summer day and the gnomon's shadow swings from west to east across the dial in the crops; at midwinter noon it is long, at midsummer noon short; under cloudCover 1 it is gone. nameAt over the cell answers with the hour. Census: one structural scalar moved, baseline re-pinned, everything else churn.
avoid: Do not put it on the roundel of the plaza (that is the fountain's). Do not draw the shadow into the cached ground — it moves every frame. Do not add a clock face: the town has a clock tower; this is the courtyard's older, slower one.
